title: What If Every Wild Salmon Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every wild salmon vanished? The forests would feel it first.
Along Pacific salmon rivers, bears haul fish into the woods. One bear can pull out five hundred to seven hundred in a season.
Bears eat about half of each fish. The rest feeds gulls, ravens, eagles, insects, and the soil.
Near salmon-rich rivers, forty to eighty percent of the nitrogen in shrubs and trees comes from the open ocean.
In forest patches without salmon, trees grow half as fast.
Take the salmon away and the forest loses a fertilizer delivered from the sea, one fish at a time.
